_note: Mechanism: sincere wrong effort. He is genuinely trying to be tidy; the method is insane. Ends on the reveal that the system has consumed the thing it was meant to simplify.

premise.situation: A man owns one pan and washes it immediately after every use so he never has washing up
premise.turn: He now plans meals around what the single pan can do and eats standing at the sink
premise.detail: he dries it and puts it away before he sits down to eat

character_sheet: a man in his thirties, short hair, plain t-shirt, small tidy kitchen

beats.text: My flatmate owns one pan. On purpose.
He says if you only own one pan you never have washing up.
Which is true. Because he washes it while the food is still cooking.
He dries it and puts it away before he has eaten anything.
He now plans his meals around what one pan can physically do.
I asked him if he wanted a second pan for his birthday.
He looked at me like I had offered him a debt.
